P18.pitch: Independent shared office by the Meguro river in Gotanda; warm reception, a range of chairs and monitors, suits a few hours of remote work.
order: Self-serve jasmine tea in the fridge
Coffee pot no longer standard; bring your own
P18.best: Weekday daytime, when the front desk is staffed and the main tables are quiet; try the chairs before settling. Weekends run shorter (10:30-19:00).
P18.workNotes: Wi-Fi, monitors and a choice of desks and chairs; credit cards accepted; weekdays 9:00-22:00. Booths at the back are used by long-stay members.
P18.headsUp: Hard to find from the street; one review complains of a heavy-handed typist in the rear booths with no staff intervention.

why.vibe: Reviews call it warmer than the usual mechanical share office, well-lit, with the river outside.
why.uniq: Independent and personable, with try-before-you-sit furniture, but the format is a standard shared office.
why.food: Jasmine tea in a fridge; the coffee pot has gone and one regular misses it.
why.work: Wi-Fi, monitors and long hours on weekdays; loses a point for noise complaints and shorter weekend hours.

quotes.text: 清潔感があり、受付の人の感じもいい。
一般的には機械的な雰囲気が多いシェアオフィスにおいて、こちらは温かみが感じられる。
キーボードの打鍵音がありえないくらい強すぎる会員の方が奥のブースによく居座るので、勘弁してほしい。

P18.summaryEn: Reviewers praise the friendly desk, cleanliness and warmth compared with chain offices, and note good internet and card payment; one complaint about a loud typist and one wish for the coffee pot to return.

P19.pitch: Quiet study-and-work studio in Nishi-Shinjuku run under the Benkyo Cafe (learning-gym) banner; wide desks, suits students and evening workers.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P19.best: Google lists weekday hours from 17:00 to 21:00 and Saturday from noon, so this is an evening and weekend room; go early on Saturday for a wide desk.
P19.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets per the source sheet; large desks that take textbooks; not 24 hours. Staff walk first-timers through the system.
P19.headsUp: Google hours (weekday evenings only) sit oddly against a ¥2,970 day cap, so check before planning a full day; one review notes stuffy air.

why.vibe: Described as calm, spacious and café-like, with a 4.6 rating.
why.uniq: A study-first room rather than an office floor, but one of several such studios.
why.food: No drink service confirmed in claims or reviews.
why.work: Wide desks and good Wi-Fi, but weekday access appears limited to evenings.

quotes.text: 机が広くて教科書を開いても全く問題なく勉強できた。
カフェのように居心地がよく、集中したい時にとても使いやすい空間でした。
空気が少しこもっている感じがしたので、そこが改善されたら言うことなしです。

P19.summaryEn: Consistently praised as quiet, spacious and easy to focus in, with helpful staff; the only gripe is slightly stale air.

P20.pitch: Small independent coworking room on the 4th floor between Shinjuku and Takadanobaba; ¥500 an hour, English-friendly staff, suits visitors and remote calls.
order: Free water, instant coffee, tea, miso soup, snacks
Blend coffee machine, ¥50 a cup
P20.best: Weekday daytime is uncrowded; there are sofas for a break as well as desks. Closed Sundays.
P20.workNotes: Outlets and Wi-Fi at every seat; monitors lent free; no booths but calls are fine with earphones; drop-in without membership; Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00.
P20.headsUp: No signage at the building entrance; take the lift to 4F. The source sheet's 24-hour claim conflicts with listed 10:00-18:00 hours.

why.vibe: Regulars single out the atmosphere and the uncramped layout with sofas.
why.uniq: Not a chain and unusually personable, though the offer is a familiar one.
why.food: Free instant coffee, tea and snacks plus a ¥50 blend machine, nothing cooked.
why.work: Outlets, Wi-Fi, free monitors and calls allowed; closes at 18:00 and Sundays.

quotes.text: 1時間500円と良心的。混雑もしておらずきれいで使いやすい。
ブースは無いがイヤホンを使えば電話OK。
ここは何より雰囲気が抜群なので一番利用しています。

P20.summaryEn: Reviews are almost uniformly positive: cheap, clean, quiet, friendly English-speaking staff, free monitors and a good atmosphere; the only friction is finding the unmarked door.

P21.pitch: Glass-fronted street-level chain coworking by Shinjuku-sanchome; no registration, drink bar, six web-meeting booths, skews 20s-30s.
order: Free drink bar: latte, cocoa, flavoured syrups, vinegar drinks
Bring your own food; no food sold
P21.best: Weekday mornings from 7:30; weekends and holidays fill up between 13:00 and 15:00 and members report being turned away.
P21.workNotes: Wi-Fi, monitors to borrow, six booths and private rooms (earphones required, 60-minute cap when busy); no membership needed; weekdays 7:30-21:30, weekends from 9:00.
P21.headsUp: Open area can be noisy and weekends often hit capacity; one 2026 review found the Wi-Fi too slow to run a speed test; toilets are the building's.

why.vibe: Clean and well-located but reviews repeatedly mention noise and crowding.
why.uniq: A standard chain outlet, distinguished mainly by the glass frontage and booth count.
why.food: Free drink bar with syrups and lattes but no food.
why.work: Long hours and booths, but weekend capacity problems and a serious Wi-Fi complaint.

quotes.text: 立地最高かつ綺麗で使いやすいけど、土日祝日13時〜15時ぐらいまでしばしば満席になる。
オープンスペースのおばさまの話し声がずっとうるさく集中できなかった。
ドリンクはカフェラテとかココアがある。

P21.summaryEn: Praised for location, cleanliness, staff and the drink bar; criticised for noise in the open area, weekend full-house turnaways and, in one recent case, unusable Wi-Fi.

P22.pitch: Plant-filled independent coworking on a 5th floor near Shinjuku west exit; Japan-shaped shared table, capsule booths, Herman Miller chairs, attached café.
order: HAPON Cafe: self-serve drinks, hand-drip coffee
Free hand-drip on Tuesdays per one review
P22.best: Weekday daytime only (Google lists 10:00-16:30); try the capsule booths or pick a chair you like at the big table.
P22.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets; calls and web meetings allowed in the open space with earphones; no phone booths; a tatami room and bookshelf; sources disagree on hours.
P22.headsUp: One 2025 review says visitor drop-in was refused, and listed hours vary from 16:30 to 19:00 across sources; confirm before travelling.

why.vibe: Wood desks, plants, an organic interior and a choice of designer chairs are what every review mentions.
why.uniq: Japan-archipelago table, capsule booths and a tatami room set it apart from office floors.
why.food: In-house café with hand-drip coffee, though self-serve.
why.work: Good desk and calls allowed, but short weekday-only hours and uncertainty over whether drop-in is still offered.

quotes.text: オープンスペースではイヤホン使用でウェブ会議・電話などもできます。
木のデスクで、観葉植物が多いため、白で統一されたような会社のオフィスとは違って雰囲気がよく気分転換になりました。
NO VISITOR DROP IN available.

P22.summaryEn: Older reviews love the atmosphere, chairs and staff; the most recent one reports that visitor drop-in was not available, so the status is unclear.

P23.pitch: Nomura's H1O serviced office floors by Nishi-Shinjuku station near the Tocho; app-controlled entry, 24 hours, quiet, suits members over casual visitors.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P23.best: Listed as 24 hours; with a single review there is nothing to say about peaks, so weekday office hours are the safe bet for reception.
P23.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets; entry and meeting-room booking via a dedicated app; meeting rooms for 2-6; drop-in reportedly possible but pricing unpublished.
P23.headsUp: No drop-in price is published and the app-based entry means you will need to register in advance; only one Google review exists.

why.vibe: Described as quiet and settled but there is no review evidence beyond the operator's line.
why.uniq: A serviced-office brand floor with app entry; little to distinguish it.
why.work: 24-hour access, Wi-Fi and outlets, but unpublished drop-in terms and app registration.

P23.summaryEn: No recent Google reviews to draw on.

P24.pitch: Singapore-born premium coworking on the 18th floor of Miraina Tower, straight off the Shinjuku ticket gates, with Gyoen views; members and tours only.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P24.best: Weekday 9:00-18:00 only; the single review praises the view, so a window seat if you ever get in.
P24.workNotes: Source sheet states drop-in is not offered; access is by membership or arranged visit. Closed weekends and holidays.
P24.headsUp: Not a drop-in venue per the source sheet; listed here for completeness. Three Google reviews only.

why.vibe: Open, clean and with a view the one reviewer did not want to leave.
why.uniq: A global chain's premium floor; the view is the distinguishing feature.
why.work: No drop-in access and office hours only, so it fails the casual-desk test.

quotes.text: 広々として開放的、 清潔感もあり 快適です
出る時に名残惜しく、もう少し座っていたいと思いました

P24.summaryEn: The single substantive review found the space spacious, clean and scenic; nothing on price or access because drop-in is not offered.

P25.pitch: Regus-run Spaces floor by Shinjuku west exit; modern lounge and private booths, event programme, aimed at members and their guests.
order: Lobby coffee shop; café latte criticised
Drinks: otherwise not confirmed
P25.best: Weekday 9:00-18:00 reception hours; the lounge by the big windows is the room reviewers like, but the meeting-room corridor gets noisy at times.
P25.workNotes: Open lounge and private booths; drop-in price not published; Google lists weekday hours only despite a 24-hour claim for members; air-conditioning after 18:00 is charged extra.
P25.headsUp: Rated 3.7 with several one-star complaints about reception manners; a Regus member reported being unable to use this site; evening air-con surcharge.

why.vibe: Bright modern interior with big windows, dragged down by reception complaints.
why.uniq: Standard Spaces branding; the old exterior versus modern interior is the only surprise.
why.food: A lobby coffee shop exists but the latte quality was called out.
why.work: No published drop-in terms, weekday reception, noise near meeting rooms and after-hours surcharges.

quotes.text: 内装は非常にモダンで洗練されており、一歩足を踏み入れるだけで仕事のスイッチが入ります。
特に18時以降の冷房利用料が高額で不満を感じました。
受付の女性の態度が悪い

P25.summaryEn: Split reviews: the interior, light and station access are praised, while reception staff, evening air-con fees, noise around meeting rooms and latte quality draw one-star ratings.

signals.crowding: noisy near meeting rooms at times

P26.pitch: nex-run THE HUB lounge inside the Shinjuku Washington Hotel building; ¥220 per 30 minutes, free drinks and monitors, 24-hour access, suits long cheap days.
order: Free drink bar (coffee machine, soft drinks)
Two convenience stores on the ground floor
P26.best: Weekday mornings after reception opens at 10:00; the underground passage from the station is open 6:00-22:45 for wet days. Weekend plans are reportedly good value.
P26.workNotes: Open lounge, sofa seats and free monitors; 24-hour access for registered users but reception only from 10:00; no individual air-con control.
P26.headsUp: Reception starts at 10:00, awkward if you forget a key or bring a guest early; the coffee machine drips into the next cup.

why.vibe: Spacious, clean and presentable to clients, but a hotel-building office lounge.
why.uniq: One of a thousand-plus nex sites; the hotel setting is the only twist.
why.food: Free drinks including a slightly leaky coffee machine; food from the convenience stores downstairs.
why.work: Monitors, free drinks, 24-hour access and a very low rate; the late reception is a minor snag.

quotes.text: 広くて快適でモニターも無料！ 飲み物も飲み放題ですごいコスパです！
受付の業務開始が10時と遅く顧客対応や鍵を忘れた場合などで困ることがある
駅からやや距離がありますが地下で来れるので雨の日でも濡れずに来れるのが良い

P26.summaryEn: Reviewers like the value, free drinks and monitors, clean rooms and friendly desk; complaints are the 10:00 reception start, lack of individual air-con and a dripping coffee machine.

P27.pitch: Upmarket compact coworking between Shinjuku west exit and Okubo; three-bean coffee, calm room, ¥550 per 30 minutes, suits founders doing paperwork.
order: Coffee from three different beans, plus iced coffee and iced tea
P27.best: Weekday daytime only (9:00-18:00, closed weekends); reviewers say it rarely gets crowded, so any seat works.
P27.workNotes: High-speed Wi-Fi and outlets; meeting rooms from 6 to 48 people; drop-in weekdays 9:00-18:00, monthly from ¥33,000.
P27.headsUp: A nine-minute walk from JR Shinjuku and closed weekends; pricey per hour compared with neighbours.

why.vibe: Clean, quiet and comfortable with a 4.8 rating; described as a place to get one's head in order.
why.uniq: The location within 500m of the Legal Affairs Bureau, tax office and post office is a genuine niche for company founders.
why.food: Coffee taken seriously, with three bean types and iced options; no food.
why.work: Fast Wi-Fi, outlets, calm and meeting rooms; weekday-only and closes at 18:00.

quotes.text: コーヒーは、違うテイストの３種類の豆を使うところにこだわりを感じました。
あまり混み合いすぎることもなく、静けさと話しやすさのバランスもちょうどいい感じ。
綺麗で静かで、ここで作業するとはかどるし気持ち的にもとても『整う』っていう感じです。

P27.summaryEn: Uniformly warm reviews for the quiet, clean room, attentive reception and good coffee; the only caveat is the walk from Shinjuku station.

P28.pitch: ACCEA Cafe chain outlet in a red building by Nishi-Shinjuku station; 24 hours with an app, free drinks, food delivery allowed, conversation and calls permitted.
order: Free drink bar (coffee, tea, cocoa, soup)
Bring your own or order Uber Eats
P28.best: Weekday mornings or late night; weekday afternoons can hit capacity and no reservations are taken. Sofa seats have 3-in-1 charging cables.
P28.workNotes: Wi-Fi good enough for Zoom; app users pay ¥132 per 15 min, others ¥209; 22:00-6:00 access needs app ID verification; booths are not soundproofed.
P28.headsUp: Calls are allowed, so expect a sales call at the next desk; cheaper rate needs the app; Google's day-by-day hours look wrong against the 24-hour claim.

why.vibe: Clean and convenient, but mostly open seating with talkers about.
why.uniq: One of two ACCEA sites in Shinjuku and a standard format; the other is said to be better laid out.
why.food: Free drinks that one reviewer rates as mediocre, but delivery and bring-your-own are welcome.
why.work: Round-the-clock, no booking, Zoom-capable Wi-Fi; loses a point for noise and unsoundproofed booths.

quotes.text: Wi-FIがありテレカン/Zoomできる
フリードリンクは微妙なので持ち込み推奨。個室ブースは遮音なし。
電話OKになっているせいか、真横で永遠に営業電話している人がいます。集中できません。

P28.summaryEn: Valued for 24-hour, no-booking access near the station with free drinks and workable Wi-Fi; marked down for noise from permitted calls, weak booth soundproofing, a broken charging cable and afternoon full houses.

P29.pitch: Kinko's-run coworking in the Shinjuku Center Building basement; ¥550 an hour, free drinks, lockers and meeting booths, cashless and weekday-only for drop-ins.
order: Free drink bar
Copy and print services on site
P29.best: Weekday mornings when the study crowd is focused; drop-in is 9:00-20:00 Monday to Friday only, with members getting 8:00-23:00 and weekends.
P29.workNotes: Prior member registration required; cashless only; free drinks, lockers, web-meeting booths and A1 poster printing; Wi-Fi reports range from 6.8Mbps to fine.
P29.headsUp: Registration before first use and no cash; a 2026 review complains of the staff door slamming repeatedly; 3.5 rating with mixed Wi-Fi reports.

why.vibe: A basement room one reviewer found unsettling and would swap for a clean net café.
why.uniq: Coworking bolted onto a print shop, so poster printing and copying are a real differentiator.
why.work: Booths, lockers and long member hours, but registration hassle, weekday-only drop-in and a door-noise complaint.

quotes.text: カフェよりコスパいいし周りは集中してる人が多いので勉強してたらあっという間でした。
スタッフの方が出入りするたびにドアが大きな音を立てながら閉められます。
コワーキングのくせにインターネットの通信速度が遅すぎる。6.8Mbpsて…

P29.summaryEn: Regulars find it cheap for the location and good for focused study; others cite a slamming staff door, slow internet at one point and an unsettled feel.

P30.pitch: Pasela's karaoke-box coworking near Higashi-Shinjuku; a private room to yourself, a drink an hour, real food menu, suits calls and long uninterrupted stints.
order: One free drink per hour from the karaoke menu
Full Pasela food menu, ordered to the room
P30.best: Weekday daytime; Google lists 11:00 opening and weekday-only work use for the matched branch, while the source sheet says 9:30-23:00. Any room is private.
P30.workNotes: Private karaoke rooms with outlets, phone cables and amenities; Wi-Fi; calls and meetings are fine behind a closed door; work use is limited to certain days and hours.
P30.headsUp: Google matched the Shinjuku Yasukuni-dori branch, not Higashi-Shinjuku, so hours and days may differ; work-use slots are restricted and weekends may be closed.

why.vibe: A dim karaoke room is calm and private rather than beautiful, but reviewers find it settling.
why.uniq: Working alone in a karaoke box with room service is a genuinely one-off format.
why.food: Real Pasela kitchen food and a wide drink list delivered to the room.
why.work: Private, outlets, cables and calls are no problem; limited work-use days and hours cost a point.

quotes.text: カラオケルームを一人で作業用途に使え、1時間に1杯ドリンク無料、かつアメニティ充実していて、使い勝手がよいです。
コンセントの利用ももちろんでき、スマホケーブルもあって充電できます。
お仕事利用ができる曜日、時間帯の制約はありますがお得で美味しい食事も頼めますし引き続き使います

P30.summaryEn: Reviewers rate it 4.8 for the private room, the hourly free drink, charging cables, good food and friendly staff; the only caveat is restricted work-use days and times.

P31.pitch: Benkyo Cafe's Shinjuku south-exit studio on a 6th floor in Yoyogi; big windows, drink bar, a studying crowd, ¥500 an hour for visitors.
order: Free drink bar with decent coffee
P31.best: Weekday evenings and weekend afternoons, which are the listed visitor hours (Mon-Fri 17:00-21:00, Sat from noon, Sun 13:00-18:00); take a window seat for the light.
P31.workNotes: Wi-Fi, no phone booths, a quieter self-study room at the back; visitor entry is hourly; the source sheet's 6:00-23:00 hours likely apply to members only.
P31.headsUp: Hours for visitors are much narrower than the 6:00-23:00 in the claims; the building is not obvious from the street; one reviewer felt regulars get preferential treatment.

why.vibe: Large windows, good seat spacing and a pleasant low hum of people working.
why.uniq: A study-café chain with a members' community rather than an office floor.
why.food: Drink bar with coffee that reviewers actually like.
why.work: Wi-Fi and calm, but no booths, no calls and short visitor hours.

quotes.text: 窓が大きくて開放的。適度な席間隔と環境音が心地いい。
ドリンクバーも付いていて長時間滞在したいと思いました。
内輪の人とそれ以外で扱いが平等ではないと感じる時あります。

P31.summaryEn: Mostly 4-5 stars for concentration, coffee, light and reasonable pricing; complaints are about staff footsteps and nail-tapping, a hard-to-find entrance and a clubby feel among regulars.

P32.pitch: Nomura Real Estate's +OURS on the 49th floor of the Shinjuku Center Building; concierge, library, phone booths, 24-hour for members; drop-in at ¥3,300 a day.
order: Drinks: self-serve available per reviews, details not confirmed
P32.best: Weekday 8:00-20:00 reception hours; the view is the draw, but reviewers say the quiet zone is closed to drop-ins, so expect the general floor.
P32.workNotes: Lounge, library, phone booths and private rooms; 24-hour claim applies to members, Google lists 8:00-20:00; drop-ins cannot enter the no-conversation zone.
P32.headsUp: Rated 3.7 with repeated complaints of loud calls, unsilenced phones and corporate groups on the open floor; booths are far from seats and thin-walled; cold reception noted.

why.vibe: 49th-floor view and polished fit-out, undermined by the crowd.
why.uniq: A well-appointed developer-run floor, but nothing you cannot find elsewhere except the height.
why.food: Nothing confirmed beyond a drinks corner.
why.work: Booths and long member hours, but noise complaints, drop-in exclusion from the quiet zone and thin booth walls.

quotes.text: 特に会話禁止のゾーンはドロップインでは入れませんので実態は契約しないと分かりません。
居酒屋並みの煩さになり、大事な商談などの途中でお互いの声が聞きづらいなどのことが度々起こった
景色はいいし綺麗なのでいい

P32.summaryEn: The view, location and hardware get credit, but recent reviews are dominated by noise from members and corporate groups, unhelpful staff and booths that are far away and thin-walled; one ex-member advises against joining.

P33.pitch: Large coworking on a 4th floor near Kyobashi, up to 92 seats with rocking-style chairs and varied seating; ¥550 an hour with a locker on weekdays.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P33.best: Weekday mornings before the resident company groups settle in; 9:00-20:00 Monday to Friday, closed weekends.
P33.workNotes: Locker included in the drop-in rate; many seat types; registration is light; ID is checked at reception; no confirmed booths.
P33.headsUp: One 2025 drop-in reports staff attempting to note the number from a My Number card; another found two company groups treating the free-address area as their office and talking constantly.

why.vibe: Attractively updated after the move, with interesting chairs, but recent visitors found it loud.
why.uniq: The seat variety and the locker-in-the-price deal give it a distinct offer.
why.food: Nothing confirmed in claims or reviews.
why.work: Lockers and ample seating, but weekday-only, an ID-handling worry and noise from resident groups.

quotes.text: 本人確認で出したマイナンバーカードのマイナンバーを控えられそうになった。
自分たちのオフィスのように振る舞って、大声で話してるので、わざわざ選ぶ必要がない施設になっている。
椅子の足が曲線になっていて、ロッキングチェアのようで面白かったです。

P33.summaryEn: Older reviews praise comfort, easy registration and the updated interior after relocation; the two most recent drop-in reviews are one and two stars over noisy company groups and a My Number handling concern.

signals.crowding: company groups can dominate open area

P34.pitch: JR Central's 11th-floor business lounge a minute from Tokyo station; Costa Coffee, borrowable kit, meeting rooms, from 20 minutes, suits pre-shinkansen work.
order: Costa Coffee, hot and iced
P34.best: Weekday 8:00-20:00; the open space looks over the Bank of Japan, so take a window seat. Book a seat on the phone before arriving.
P34.workNotes: Bookable from 20 minutes via smartphone; loan equipment and meeting rooms; five minutes to car 16 of the Tokaido shinkansen; closed weekends.
P34.headsUp: No published drop-in rate in the claims; some users arrive on JR Tokai tour packages, so seats may be tied to bookings.

why.vibe: Calm interior with a view over the Bank of Japan and a 4.7 rating.
why.uniq: A railway-run lounge timed around shinkansen departures is a specific idea.
why.food: Costa Coffee counter with iced options.
why.work: Polite reception, rooms and kit, but weekday-only and priced by short slots.

quotes.text: オープンスペースは日本銀行を見渡せるので、良い景色を見ながら仕事が出来る
新幹線乗車前の隙間時間に利用できて便利です。
アイスコーヒーなども飲むことができ言うことナシの素晴らしい環境でした。

P34.summaryEn: Reviewers like the station access, polite reception, view, coffee and the ability to use short gaps before a shinkansen; no complaints in the sample.
